data.headline: Stock up 4 weeks now to lock in current costs before tariffs bite harder
data.why: Two fresh 10% China tariffs stack on your Guangdong supply chain. The plan adds four weeks of inventory now, shielding the 86% of cost exposed to China from the next hike. Simulation shows the figures above in extra profit versus doing nothing, with zero price change and full sell-through.
data.watch_out: Cash dips to the figures above at peak outlay; if a third tariff wave or freight spike hits before week 13 payback, liquidity gets tight. Monitor customs notices and container rates weekly.
data.recheck_when: Next USTR tariff announcement or freight index jump above current level

what_happened.text: The fentanyl-related duty on Chinese goods rose from 10% to 20%.
A 10% baseline tariff on all imports took effect, so Chinese goods paid 30% in total.
The country rate on China rose to 84% (executive order of April 8), for 104% in total.
The rate on China rose to 125% (executive order of April 9), for 145% in total.
After talks in Geneva the US cut the reciprocal rate on China to 10%, keeping the 20% fentanyl duty: 30% in total.
The US and China extended the pause on the higher reciprocal rates to November 10; the 30% total stayed.

caveats: The path is the extra duty by date, applied when goods enter the US: an order placed in week t pays the rate in force 5 weeks later. The cost rise is (1 + duty then) / (1 + 20% at the as-of date) − 1, on the part of the landed cost that scales with the duty (set at 86%: $9.00 of goods at $12.50 landed). The $9.00 goods cost, the $1.40 freight and the made-up shop are the owner's figures, not data.

Only the extra duties of this timeline are in the path. Section 301 duties (7.5% to 25% on many Chinese kitchenware lines, depending on the product code) were already in force and are not added; they would make the real rise a few points smaller. Steel and aluminium kitchenware faced separate Section 232 duties; this case is silicone and bamboo. Ending de minimis for China (May 2) does not touch bulk sea freight. No product exemption we found covered kitchenware.

Goods already on the water on 25 Mar that arrived after 9 Apr also paid the higher duty in real life; the engine charges that stock its old cost. Rivals face the same duty here (their cost moves too).

The model has seen this period. Nemotron Ultra's model card gives a pre-training cutoff of September 2025 and a post-training cutoff of May 2026, so a date in the prompt cannot make it forget. The run only gives it news from before the date, and the leak check looks for hindsight in what it wrote.

“Best plan in hindsight” is the best of about 230 plans on a fixed grid (price, start, end, extra stock), run on the real path. Shoppers react to a sweep plan like they did to the nearest price plan the analysis tested; with none tested, they are neutral.
News pages are read as they are today. Any article that names a date after the as-of date is dropped, but a page edited later could still carry hindsight.

A plan that switches supplier is scored with the share of the price rise that Ultra assumed the alternative supplier would feel (`alt_shock_exposure`). The real price path says nothing about whether another supplier would really have been shielded, so those plans' results rest on that assumption.
